meta.title: Trigeneration screening for Tunisian hotels
meta.description: One gas engine on site makes electricity, hot water and cooling. Find out in two minutes whether it would pay for your hotel, with honest ranges and cited sources.

hero.title: Make your own energy.
hero.lede: One gas engine on site makes electricity, hot water and the heat that runs an absorption chiller. Our free screening tool tells you in two minutes whether your hotel is a fit, and says so plainly when it isn't.
hero.ringsCaption: What a {kwe} kWe plant covers for a {rooms}-room Djerba hotel, over a full year.

payback.body: Years to earn back the plant

demo.legend: Each rail runs from the favourable to the unfavourable case, with the central case marked. They are the choices an enthusiastic installer and a sceptical juror would make, not statistical bounds.
demo.fte: With the FTE subsidy, payback could fall to {range}. Hotel eligibility is not confirmed, so it never enters the headline.

flow.title: One engine. Three jobs.
flow.lede: A normal hotel buys power from STEG and burns gas for hot water. More than half of a power station's fuel leaves as waste heat. Trigeneration catches that heat on your site and uses it.

gas.label: Step 1
gas.title: Gas in.
gas.body: From the STEG gas network that most coastal hotel zones already have.

power.label: Step 2
power.title: Power on site.
power.body: About {pct}% of the gas becomes electricity the hotel uses directly.

heat.label: Step 3
heat.title: Heat, recovered.
heat.body: Another {pct}% comes back as hot water for rooms, kitchen, laundry and the pool, all year.

cold.label: Step 4
cold.title: Heat becomes cold.
cold.body: In summer, an absorption chiller turns spare heat into chilled water for air conditioning.

honesty.title: Most hotels will hear “not yet”.
honesty.lede: The tool is a screening tool. It is built to find the few hotels where a plant pays, and to say so plainly everywhere else.
honesty.signs: It tends to pay where a hotel is large, open all year, has a heated pool or spa and is on the gas network.

big.title: {rooms} rooms, Djerba, pool
big.note: Open all year, big hot-water load. Worth a study.

desert.title: {rooms} rooms, Tozeur, pool
desert.note: Hot summers, and cold desert nights for the pool. Worth a study.

small.title: {rooms} rooms, Djerba, no pool
small.note: Too little heat demand in winter. The engine would sit idle.

screen.title: Screen your hotel.
screen.lede: Three answers: rooms, city and pool. The full tool adds your electricity price, an hourly dashboard and a PDF report.
screen.card: Start with the Djerba demo hotel, then change it to yours.

tornado.title: What moves the answer.
tornado.lede: The Djerba case pays back in about {years} years in the central case. Here is how far each input moves it, one at a time.
tornado.quote: One installer quote matters more than every other input combined. That is what a feasibility study gets you.

services.title: From a screening to a plant.
services.lede: The tool is free. When it says “possible fit”, we take it from estimate to evidence.

study.title: Feasibility study.
study.body: We replace our assumptions with your numbers: your STEG bills, a site visit and installer quotes.

referral.title: Installer referral.
referral.body: We introduce you to Tunisian installers who have built CHP plants, and compare their quotes line by line.

esco.title: Shared savings.
esco.body: A partner finances, owns and runs the plant. The hotel pays from the savings, with no upfront cost.

proof.title: Already running in Tunisia.
proof.lede: Not in hotels yet. In factories, for years.

final.title: Possible fit?
final.lede: Send us your screening result. A member of the team replies within two working days with what a study would cost for your hotel.
